title_ar: كلمة الشيخ في مؤتمر الاتجاهات الفكرية بين حرية التعبير و محكمات الشريعة
title_en: The Sheikh's Address at the Conference on Intellectual Currents Between Freedom of Expression and the Firm Principles of the Sharia
body_ar:
افتتحت صباح اليوم الاثنين 20 جمادى الآخر الموافق 19 مارس 2017م ، بمكة المركز مؤتمر الاتجاهات الفكرية بين حرية التعبير و محكمات الشريعة الذي ينظمه المجمع الفقهي التابع لرابطة العالم الإسلامي و الذي يستمر لمدة يومين

و المجمع عبارة عن هيئة علمية إسلامية ذات شخصية اعتبارية مستقلة ، داخل إطار رابطة العالم الاسلامي، مكونة من مجموعة مختارة من فقهاء الأمة الإسلامية و علمائها.

و يهدف المجمع لمجموعة من الأهداف النبيلة و التي من أبرزها :

- بيان الأحكام الشرعية فيما يواجه المسلمين في أنحاء العالم من مشكلات و نوازل و قضايا مستجدة من مصادر التشريع الاسلامي المعتبرة

- إبراز تفوق الفقه الاسلامي على القوانين الوضعية و إثبات شمول الشريعة و استجابتها لحل كل القضايا التي تواجه الأمة الإسلامية في كل زمان و مكان ...

و قد ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو حفظه الله تعالى كلمة مختصرة قال فيها
body_en:
This Monday morning, 20 Jumada al-Akhirah, corresponding to 19 March 2017, there opened in Mecca the Conference on Intellectual Currents Between Freedom of Expression and the Firm Principles of the Sharia, organised by the Islamic Fiqh Academy attached to the Muslim World League, which runs for two days.

The Academy is an Islamic scholarly body with an independent legal personality, within the framework of the Muslim World League, made up of a select group of the jurists and scholars of the Islamic community.

The Academy pursues a set of noble aims, the most prominent of which are:

- To set out the rulings of the Sharia on the problems, novel cases and newly arising questions that Muslims face in all parts of the world, from the recognised sources of Islamic law

- To bring out the superiority of Islamic fiqh over man-made laws, and to establish the comprehensiveness of the Sharia and its capacity to answer and resolve every question facing the Islamic community in every time and place …

His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him) delivered a brief address in which he said

flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY (addendum section 10, applied to a news record). The title promises 'The Sheikh's Address', and the body breaks off at the exact words 'a brief address in which he said' — the address itself is not in the record at all. What precedes it is a description of the Islamic Fiqh Academy's aims, written by the Academy or the site, NOT by the Sheikh. A reader landing on this page in English will take the Academy's stated aims — including the claim of Islamic fiqh's superiority over man-made law — for the content of the Sheikh's address. The address exists only in the embedded video. This record must not be rendered as an address of the Sheikh's.

flags.note: EDITORIALLY SENSITIVE, and NOT THE SHEIKH'S WORDS. This is the Academy's own statement of its aims as the site reproduces it. In English it reads as a programmatic claim against secular legal systems. Attribution must survive into the display, or the sentence will be read as the Sheikh's.

options: the firm principles of the Sharia
the definitive rulings of the Sharia
flags.note: محكم is glossed in the project glossary as 'of clear import', in the Qur'anic muḥkam/mutashābih pairing. In this title محكمات is used more loosely for the Sharia's settled, non-negotiable principles. 'Of clear import' would be unidiomatic in a conference title; the rendering chosen keeps the sense but not the glossary's form, so it is flagged.
